ports.name: a_req_i.ben

ports.evidence: x_req_o.src <= a_req_i.src when (sel = '0') else b_req_i.src.

ports.evidence: x_req_o.amoop <= a_req_i.amoop when (sel = '0') else b_req_i.amoop.

ports.evidence: x_req_o.lock <= a_req_i.lock when (sel = '0') else b_req_i.lock.

ports.evidence: x_req_o.fence <= a_req_i.fence or b_req_i.fence.

ports.evidence: x_rsp_i fields are used in FSM (x_rsp_i.ack) and in concurrent assignments to a_rsp_o.* and b_rsp_o.*.

signals.name: state
signals.functionality: Holds the current FSM state (S_IDLE, S_BUSY_A, S_BUSY_B); used as the case selector in the combinational FSM and is updated on clock from state_nxt to drive arbiter behaviour.
signals.evidence: state assigned in arbiter_sync (state <= state_nxt) and used as case state in arbiter_fsm; state = S_BUSY_* conditions gate a_req/b_req updates.

signals.name: state_nxt
signals.functionality: Holds the combinationally computed next FSM state (derived from state and request/response inputs) and is the value captured into state on the next clock edge.
signals.evidence: state_nxt <= state default then modified in arbiter_fsm case branches; state <= state_nxt on rising_edge(clk_i).

signals.name: a_req
signals.functionality: Latches whether A has an outstanding request across cycles (captured from a_req_i.stb or retained); the FSM tests a_req to decide grants when external stb is absent.
signals.evidence: a_req <= a_req or a_req_i.stb in arbiter_sync; a_req tested in arbiter_fsm conditions to choose state_nxt and sel.

signals.name: b_req
signals.functionality: Latches whether B has an outstanding request across cycles (captured from b_req_i.stb or retained); the FSM tests b_req to decide grants when external stb is absent.
signals.evidence: b_req <= b_req or b_req_i.stb in arbiter_sync; b_req tested in arbiter_fsm conditions to choose state_nxt and sel.

signals.name: sel
signals.functionality: Combinationally selects which port (A when '0', B when '1') drives the x_req_o outputs for the current arbitration decision; its value is captured into sel_q on the clock edge.
signals.evidence: sel assigned in arbiter_fsm; concurrent assignments use sel to choose between a_req_i.* and b_req_i.* and to gate a/b rsp ack/err.

signals.name: sel_q
signals.functionality: Holds the previous-cycle sel value (captured from sel) and is used by the FSM's round-robin logic to bias next arbitration decisions, thereby influencing which port is favored next.
signals.evidence: sel_q <= sel in arbiter_sync; sel_q used in arbiter_fsm condition (if sel_q = '1' or not ROUND_ROBIN_EN) then ... to choose priority.

signals.name: stb
signals.functionality: Combinationally carries the strobe to forward to x_req_o.stb; it is driven from FSM decisions and directly from selected port's stb when locked, so it reflects the active forwarded request cycle.
signals.evidence: stb assigned in arbiter_fsm (stb <= '0' default; stb <= a_req_i.stb or b_req_i.stb or '1' in branches); x_req_o.stb <= stb.

signals.name: locked
signals.functionality: Holds the two-bit latched lock state captured from locked_nxt each cycle; its per-bit values are checked in busy branches to decide whether to forward stb or to rely on per-port lock semantics.
signals.evidence: locked <= locked_nxt in arbiter_sync; arbiter_fsm checks locked(0)/locked(1) in S_BUSY_* branches to choose stb and state transitions.

signals.name: locked_nxt
signals.functionality: Combinationally computes the next locked vector as the concatenation/combination of the current inputs (locked default then b_req_i.lock & a_req_i.lock) and is captured into locked on the next clock edge.
signals.evidence: locked_nxt <= locked default then locked_nxt <= b_req_i.lock & a_req_i.lock in others branch; locked <= locked_nxt on rising_edge.

signals.name: port_sel
signals.functionality: Holds the per-port decode bits computed from address comparisons and enable flags; used to mask per-port stb and to derive keeper.halt.
signals.evidence: concurrent assignments port_sel(0..3) <= '1' when ...; used in request process and bus_monitor

signals.name: port_req
signals.functionality: Holds the candidate request for each port, built from req_i or terminated default and with stb masked by port_sel; drives the external a/b/c/x request outputs.
signals.evidence: request process assigns port_req(i) and concurrent mappings a_req_o <= port_req(0) etc

signals.name: port_rsp
signals.functionality: Receives each external port's response (assigned from a_rsp_i..x_rsp_i) and provides the inputs that the response process OR-aggregates into int_rsp.
signals.evidence: concurrent mappings port_rsp(i) <= a/b/c/x_rsp_i and response process reads port_rsp to build tmp_v then int_rsp

signals.name: int_rsp
signals.functionality: Carries the OR-aggregated response built from port_rsp entries (data, ack, err) and supplies rsp_o fields and bus_monitor with combined status.
signals.evidence: response process builds tmp_v from port_rsp then int_rsp <= tmp_v; rsp_o.* <= int_rsp.* assignments and bus_monitor reads int_rsp.ack

signals.name: int_rsp.ack
signals.functionality: Carries the OR of all port_rsp(i).ack values into int_rsp.ack and is used both to form rsp_o.ack and to influence keeper busy release in bus_monitor.
signals.evidence: response process ORs port_rsp(i).ack into tmp_v.ack; int_rsp.ack used in bus_monitor condition and rsp_o.ack assignment

signals.name: int_rsp.err
signals.functionality: Carries the OR of all port_rsp(i).err values into int_rsp.err and is combined into rsp_o.err.
signals.evidence: response process ORs port_rsp(i).err into tmp_v.err; rsp_o.err <= int_rsp.err or keeper.err

signals.name: int_rsp.data
signals.functionality: Carries the OR-aggregated data from all port_rsp entries into int_rsp.data and forwards it to rsp_o.data.
signals.evidence: response process ORs port_rsp(i).data into tmp_v.data; int_rsp.data forwarded to rsp_o.data

signals.name: keeper
signals.functionality: Aggregates keeper.busy, lock, cnt, err, halt fields into one record used to track request timeout and locking; groups the monitor registers.
signals.evidence: keeper declared as record and bus_monitor process assigns its fields

signals.name: keeper.busy
signals.functionality: Holds whether a request is outstanding; captured from req_i.stb when free and cleared on ack, lock-release or timeout; gates which bus_monitor branch executes.
signals.evidence: keeper.busy <= req_i.stb when keeper.busy='0' in bus_monitor; if (keeper.busy='0') branch governs other assignments

signals.name: keeper.lock
signals.functionality: Captures the request lock bit when a request starts and is later tested with req_i.lock to decide early release of busy.
signals.evidence: keeper.lock <= req_i.lock in bus_monitor; ((keeper.lock = '1') and (req_i.lock = '0')) condition clears keeper.busy

signals.name: keeper.cnt
signals.functionality: Counts cycles while busy by incrementing itself each clock; its top bit is tested for timeout and used to set keeper.err.
signals.evidence: keeper.cnt <= std_ulogic_vector(unsigned(keeper.cnt) + 1) in bus_monitor; keeper.cnt(...) tested to set keeper.err

signals.name: keeper.err
signals.functionality: Captured error flag set on timeout and cleared each cycle; is ORed into rsp_o.ack and rsp_o.err to report error externally.
signals.evidence: keeper.err set in bus_monitor on timeout; rsp_o.ack/err include keeper.err in OR

signals.name: keeper.halt
signals.functionality: Captures the MSB of port_sel each clock to indicate the selected port halt condition and is tested before declaring timeout.
signals.evidence: keeper.halt <= port_sel(port_sel'left) in bus_monitor; (keeper.halt = '0') used with keeper.cnt top bit before setting keeper.err

signals.name: dev_req
signals.functionality: Provides an array of per-device request records: each dev_req(i) is driven either from main_req (with stb gated by address match) when enabled or from a terminate constant when disabled; supplies device request ports.
role: combines host input into per-device outputs
signals.evidence: bus_request generate: dev_req(i) <= main_req; disabled branch assigns req_terminate_c; concurrent assignments bind dev_req(i) to dev_x_req_o.

signals.name: dev_rsp
signals.functionality: Collects external device responses into an array; each dev_rsp(i) is driven from the corresponding dev_x_rsp_i port and is read by the response aggregator to form main_rsp.
signals.evidence: Concurrent assignments dev_rsp(i) <= dev_x_rsp_i map port inputs into dev_rsp; bus_response process reads dev_rsp(i) fields.

signals.name: main_req
signals.functionality: Receives the (optionally registered) host request from the bus register instance (neorv32_bus_reg_inst.device_req_o) and supplies that request to per-device generators; its addr slice gates which device sees stb.
signals.evidence: Instance port map device_req_o => main_req provides value; bus_request process uses main_req and its addr slice to build dev_req(i).stb.

signals.name: main_req.addr
signals.functionality: Holds the address vector of the internal host request; the addr slice is compared to each device base to select which device's stb is enabled for the forwarded request.
signals.evidence: Condition in bus_request process: main_req.addr(addr_hi_c downto addr_lo_c) = dev_base_list_c(i)(addr_hi_c downto addr_lo_c) gates dev_req(i).stb assignment.

signals.name: main_req.data
signals.functionality: Carries the request data field from the host (via instance) into the per-device request copy; forwarded into each enabled dev_req(i) by the request generator.
signals.evidence: bus_request process assigns dev_req(i) <= main_req, which forwards the data field into dev_req.

signals.name: main_req.ben
signals.functionality: Carries the byte-enable bits from the host request into the per-device request copies; forwarded unchanged into dev_req entries.
signals.evidence: dev_req(i) <= main_req in bus_request process forwards ben field to dev_req.

signals.name: main_req.stb
signals.functionality: Supplies the strobe bit used to signal a valid request; it is forwarded into dev_req(i) and is explicitly used to set dev_req(i).stb when the device base matches, otherwise dev_req(i).stb is '0'.
signals.evidence: bus_request process: dev_req(i) <= main_req; dev_req(i).stb <= main_req.stb when address matches, else '0'.

signals.name: main_req.rw
signals.functionality: Carries the read/write indicator from the host request and forwards it into per-device request copies.
signals.evidence: dev_req(i) <= main_req in bus_request process forwards rw field to dev_req.

signals.name: main_req.src
signals.functionality: Carries the source bit from the host request and forwards it into per-device request copies.
signals.evidence: dev_req(i) <= main_req in bus_request process forwards src field to dev_req.

signals.name: main_req.priv
signals.functionality: Carries the privilege bit from the host request and forwards it into per-device request copies.
signals.evidence: dev_req(i) <= main_req in bus_request process forwards priv field to dev_req.

signals.name: main_req.debug
signals.functionality: Carries the debug bit from the host request and forwards it into per-device request copies.
signals.evidence: dev_req(i) <= main_req in bus_request process forwards debug field to dev_req.

signals.name: main_req.amo
signals.functionality: Carries the atomic-op indicator from the host request and forwards it into per-device request copies.
signals.evidence: dev_req(i) <= main_req in bus_request process forwards amo field to dev_req.

signals.name: main_req.amoop
signals.functionality: Carries the AMO operation code bits from the host request and forwards them into per-device request copies.
signals.evidence: dev_req(i) <= main_req in bus_request process forwards amoop field to dev_req.

signals.name: main_req.lock
signals.functionality: Carries the lock bit from the host request and forwards it into per-device request copies.
signals.evidence: dev_req(i) <= main_req in bus_request process forwards lock field to dev_req.

signals.name: main_req.fence
signals.functionality: Carries the fence control bit from the host request and forwards it into per-device request copies.
signals.evidence: dev_req(i) <= main_req in bus_request process forwards fence field to dev_req.

signals.name: main_rsp
signals.functionality: Produces the host response by aggregating per-device responses: the bus_response process ORs dev_rsp(i).data/ack/err into tmp_v and assigns that to main_rsp, which is then presented to the bus register instance input.
signals.evidence: bus_response process builds tmp_v by ORing dev_rsp(i) fields and then main_rsp <= tmp_v; port map connects device_rsp_i => main_rsp.

signals.name: main_rsp.ack
signals.functionality: Carries the OR of device ack bits into the host response ack field; derived by OR-ing dev_rsp(i).ack across enabled devices.
signals.evidence: bus_response process ORs dev_rsp(i).ack into tmp_v.ack then main_rsp <= tmp_v; main_rsp is mapped to instance device_rsp_i.

signals.name: main_rsp.err
signals.functionality: Carries the OR of device error bits into the host response err field; derived by OR-ing dev_rsp(i).err across enabled devices.
signals.evidence: bus_response process ORs dev_rsp(i).err into tmp_v.err then main_rsp <= tmp_v; main_rsp is mapped to instance device_rsp_i.

signals.name: main_rsp.data
signals.functionality: Carries the OR-reduction of device response data words into the host response data field; derived by OR-ing dev_rsp(i).data across enabled devices and assigned to main_rsp.data.
signals.evidence: bus_response process: tmp_v.data := tmp_v.data or dev_rsp(i).data in loop; then main_rsp <= tmp_v; main_rsp mapped to instance device_rsp_i.

signals.name: arbiter
signals.functionality: Holds the AMO FSM state, captured command, read and write data; it is updated each clock from arbiter_nxt and its fields control sys_req_o selections and core responses.
signals.evidence: arbiter <= arbiter_nxt on rising_edge(clk_i) in arbiter_sync

signals.name: arbiter.state
signals.functionality: Captures the next FSM state from arbiter_nxt.state at the clock edge; the stored state selects muxes for sys_req_o fields and core_rsp_o outputs.
signals.evidence: arbiter <= arbiter_nxt (clock); concurrent when expressions use (arbiter.state = S_WRITE/S_IDLE/etc.) to choose outputs

signals.name: arbiter.cmd
signals.functionality: Holds the AMO opcode captured from arbiter_nxt.cmd; its low bits select the ALU operation executed into alu_res.
signals.evidence: arbiter <= arbiter_nxt in clocked process; amo_alu uses case arbiter.cmd(2 downto 0)

signals.name: arbiter.rdata
signals.functionality: Holds the read data captured from arbiter_nxt.rdata (from sys_rsp_i.data) and supplies operands to comparisons, the ALU, and the core response when not idle.
signals.evidence: arbiter <= arbiter_nxt (clock); cmp_opa <= ... arbiter.rdata; alu_res cases use unsigned(arbiter.rdata)

signals.name: arbiter.wdata
signals.functionality: Holds the write-data captured from arbiter_nxt.wdata (from core_req_i.data) and supplies operands to the ALU and comparison operand generation.
signals.evidence: arbiter <= arbiter_nxt (clock); cmp_opb <= ... arbiter.wdata; amo_alu uses arbiter.wdata in cases

signals.name: arbiter_nxt
signals.functionality: Combinational next-state record that is initialized from arbiter then modified by core_req_i and sys_rsp_i to produce the next FSM state, cmd, rdata and wdata.
signals.evidence: arbiter_comb: arbiter_nxt <= arbiter; fields set from core_req_i and sys_rsp_i inside case on arbiter.state

signals.name: arbiter_nxt.state
signals.functionality: Holds the computed next FSM state derived from current arbiter.state, core_req_i conditions and sys_rsp_i.ack; it determines the arbiter's next-mode to be captured on the clock edge.
signals.evidence: arbiter_comb sets arbiter_nxt.state per case S_IDLE/S_READ_WAIT/... using core_req_i and sys_rsp_i conditions

signals.name: arbiter_nxt.cmd
signals.functionality: Carries the next AMO opcode, defaulting from arbiter or captured from core_req_i.amoop when an AMO is started.
signals.evidence: arbiter_nxt <= arbiter then arbiter_nxt.cmd <= core_req_i.amoop in S_IDLE branch

signals.name: arbiter_nxt.rdata
signals.functionality: Carries read data sampled from the system response (sys_rsp_i.data) into the arbiter next-record when in READ_WAIT; otherwise preserves arbiter.rdata.
signals.evidence: in S_READ_WAIT: arbiter_nxt.rdata <= sys_rsp_i.data; arbiter_nxt <= arbiter as default

signals.name: arbiter_nxt.wdata
signals.functionality: Carries the core's write data into the arbiter next-record when an AMO is initiated, otherwise defaults from arbiter.
signals.evidence: in S_IDLE: arbiter_nxt.wdata <= core_req_i.data; arbiter_nxt <= arbiter as default

signals.name: alu_res
signals.functionality: Computes and stores the AMO ALU result on the clock edge from functions of arbiter.rdata, arbiter.wdata and cmp_res according to arbiter.cmd; drives sys_req_o.data during write phases.
signals.evidence: amo_alu process (rising_edge) assigns alu_res using case on arbiter.cmd and expressions with arbiter.rdata/wdata or cmp_res

signals.name: cmp_opa
signals.functionality: Constructs the signed-extended operand A from arbiter.rdata and the sign bit selected by arbiter.cmd(3); it is consumed by the signed less-than comparison.
signals.evidence: cmp_opa <= (arbiter.rdata(arbiter.rdata'left) and arbiter.cmd(3)) & arbiter.rdata

signals.name: cmp_opb
signals.functionality: Constructs the signed-extended operand B from arbiter.wdata and the sign bit selected by arbiter.cmd(3); it is consumed by the signed less-than comparison.
signals.evidence: cmp_opb <= (arbiter.wdata(arbiter.wdata'left) and arbiter.cmd(3)) & arbiter.wdata

signals.name: cmp_less
signals.functionality: Reflects the result of the signed less-than comparison between cmp_opa and cmp_opb and is then used to choose cmp_res.
signals.evidence: cmp_less <= '1' when (signed(cmp_opa) < signed(cmp_opb)) else '0'

signals.name: cmp_res
signals.functionality: Selects between the lower 32 bits of cmp_opa or cmp_opb based on cmp_less xor arbiter.cmd(0) and provides the fallback ALU result for certain AMO operations.
signals.evidence: cmp_res <= cmp_opa(31 downto 0) when ((cmp_less xor arbiter.cmd(0)) = '1') else cmp_opb(31 downto 0)

signals.name: state
signals.functionality: Holds the two-bit FSM state across clock edges; the case selection governs which state transitions occur based on core_req_i and rvso, and state(1) is tested elsewhere to gate strobe and sc_fail.
role: drives gating of sys_req_o.stb and sc_fail
signals.evidence: state is assigned inside rvs_control clocked process (case state ... state <= "11"/"00"/"10"); state(1) used in bus_request and sc_result.

signals.name: rvso
signals.functionality: Is a combinational signal that indicates an AMO RVS-type operation (core_req_i.amo and amoop(3 downto 2) = "10"); it gates state transitions and influences sys_req_o.stb and is an input to sc_fail.
signals.evidence: rvso <= '1' when (core_req_i.amo = '1') and (core_req_i.amoop(3 downto 2) = "10") else '0'; rvso used in rvs_control, bus_request and sc_result.

signals.name: sc_fail
signals.functionality: Captures a boolean indicating SC failure on the rising clock edge from an expression of rvso, core_req_i.stb, core_req_i.rw and state(1); it then contributes to core_rsp_o.ack and core_rsp_o.data.
role: feeds core response ack and data
signals.evidence: sc_fail assigned in sc_result clocked process: sc_fail <= rvso and core_req_i.stb and core_req_i.rw and (not state(1)); sc_fail used in core_rsp_o assignments.
